answer.text: Tax rates are the same for all industries so analysis is unnecessary
Different industries may have different tax incentives, duties, or GST rates that significantly impact profitability
Taxes are only relevant for government-owned companies
Industry analysis should completely ignore taxation

explanation.text: The Logic: Taxation varies by industry — examples include fat tax, varying GST slabs, R&D deduction encouragement, reduced alternative corporate tax schemes, excise/VAT/customs duty, road tax, stamp duty, and STT impacts by sector. These directly impact profitability and competitive dynamics. The Trap: Taxes are not uniform and affect all companies, not just government-owned ones. Ignoring taxation would lead to incomplete industry analysis. Note: Governments use taxes to encourage or discourage businesses; changes in excise, customs, or stamp duty can materially affect specific industries.
